findings.claim: The three newly encoded MCP senders (ask, clip_url, clip_pasted) have no behavioral test in mcp-server's own suite that uses a non-ASCII drive. The only check that fails if the encoding is reverted is the source scan in the frontend test suite.
findings.impact: No user-visible defect today. If someone reverts encodeURIComponent in mcp-server/src/tools/ask.ts:60 or write.ts:418/446, the mcp-server vitest job stays green, and only the frontend job catches it. A sender written in a form the scan regex does not match (for example a helper returning the raw drive, or headers.set) would pass both suites.
findings.evidence: mcp-server/src/__tests__/ask.test.ts:30,39 sends drive 'media' and expects the header 'media'. encodeURIComponent('media') === 'media', so that assertion cannot tell encoded from raw. No test file under mcp-server/src/__tests__ asserts the X-Lit-Drive header for clip_url or clip_pasted (grep for X-Lit-Drive in mcp-server shows none). Sibling tools do have such tests: read.test.ts:264-269, searchTools.test.ts:142-147, readDocument.test.ts:125-130. frontend/src/__tests__/driveHeaderEncoding.test.ts:19 now scans mcp-server/src, and .github/workflows/ci.yml has no path filters, so the frontend job runs on every change and the scan does catch a plain revert.
findings.repro: Mutation in thought: revert ask.ts:60 to `{ "X-Lit-Drive": drive }`. Result: ask.test.ts passes. driveHeaderEncoding.test.ts 'sends no raw drive name' fails and reports mcp-server/src/tools/ask.ts:60. Not run.

bucket_proposal.reason: No invariant is declared and the production code is correct. The gap is that the MCP package's own tests do not cover these senders, which matches the existing pattern for other MCP tools only partly.

findings.proposed_fix: Add a 動画 case to mcp-server/src/__tests__/ask.test.ts, and an equivalent test for clip_url and clip_pasted, asserting headers equal { 'X-Lit-Drive': encodeURIComponent('動画') }, in the same way as read.test.ts:264.

specification_compliance: No invariants file exists, so there is no declared touch-point list. The fix commit 03a007848 reaches mcp-server/src/tools/ask.ts and write.ts plus one ROOTS entry in the scan test, which is the scope r1's R1-scan-scope-mcp proposed.

The receivers decode exactly once. The core proxy unquotes the header only for its own policy check (backend/app/routers/addon_proxy.py:495-498). The intelligence addon unquotes in require_drive (addons/intelligence/app/drive_context.py:30), and the image-query routes in vision.py:271,315,373,394 depend on that function. The knowledge clip routes unquote in _require_drive (addons/knowledge/app/routers/clips.py:103), which is used at :229 and :278. Encoding at the senders is therefore correct, and ASCII names arrive unchanged.

After the fix, every non-test X-Lit-Drive sender in TypeScript (frontend/src, mcp-server/src, addons/*/frontend) uses encodeURIComponent. The iOS sender is out of the scan's scope and was reported as already encoding in r1.
potential_unspecified_behavior: The scan regex matches only the object-literal form `"X-Lit-Drive": value`, and it accepts any value that starts with `encodeURIComponent(`. A grep of non-test .ts/.tsx/.js files found no headers.set('X-Lit-Drive') or bracket-assignment senders today.
regression_risks: A drive name that contains a literal '%' sent through ask or clip_* used to be unquoted by the receiver and so arrived corrupted. It now round-trips correctly, so this is a fix, not a regression.

Because the scan test lives in the frontend package and now reads mcp-server/src through a relative path (../../..), a CI job that checks out only frontend/ would make it skip mcp-server silently. readdirSync on a missing root would throw rather than skip, though, so a missing directory would fail loudly.
test_coverage: imageQuery.driveHeader.test.ts kills reverts of both imageQuery.ts encodings: new Headers() throws on 動画, and the exact encoded value is asserted.
driveHeaderEncoding.test.ts now kills a revert at mcp-server/src/tools/ask.ts:60 and write.ts:418,446.
mcp-server's own tests do not distinguish encoded from raw for ask, clip_url or clip_pasted (see R2-mcp-encoding-only-guarded-by-scan).
not_verified: I did not run any test suite. The mutation outcomes come from reading the code.

I did not check whether GlobalSearch.imageQuery.test.tsx or ImageQueryView.test.tsx (via helpers/imageQuery.ts:52) use a non-ASCII drive whose expected header value would have to change. ImageQueryView.test.tsx:342 expects 'media', which is the same encoded or raw.
I did not confirm that the frontend CI job checks out mcp-server/ so that the scan can read it.
trajectory: There was one fix round after r1 (03a007848). It applied the existing encodeURIComponent convention to three more call sites and added one directory to the scan's ROOTS. It adds no new branch, state or prediction: the same mechanical transform and the same scan are extended in scope. 94711b140 and 4c61d2863 are review-record commits only. The design is not being patched; the fix completes a convention that already existed rather than layering conditions on it.
